routing (preset opus-led): seats you can spawn, with their model and default effort.
- driver: claude-opus-5-5, medium by default. the session the user talks to.
- engineer: claude-sonnet-5-5, high by default. writes and changes code in the area it owns and checks its own work.
- scout: claude-sonnet-5-5, medium by default. reads and searches so you do not have to; reports what it found with exact paths.
- reviewer: claude-fable-5-1, high by default. reviews and verifies someone else's work on a different model than the author.
- bulk: claude-sonnet-5-5, low by default. long mechanical reads and rewrites where judgment is cheap.
off limits: claude-opus-5-5 never runs at xhigh; claude-sonnet-5-5 never runs at max.
a spawn picks a seat, not a model, and may pass an effort within those limits; the seat default applies otherwise.
delegation:
- a child protects your context: reads and log digs you would not want in your own window go to a scout.
- disjoint pieces of work run in parallel, one writer per area.
- review and verification are independent when they run on a different seat from the author, ideally a different model; a reviewer can write the check before the engineer starts.
- long watches (builds, test suites, dev servers) are background jobs with notify, not agents.
- the decision on the critical path stays with you; read what shapes the plan yourself.
- work that continues what an existing agent did goes to that agent with message; it keeps its context, a new spawn starts cold.
- a brief carries the goal, the constraints, the definition of done, the files it owns and the report shape. the stronger the seat, the shorter the brief.
- when only children or jobs remain, end your turn; their reports wake you.
